faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find quick answers to common questions about Solidis. Can't find what you're looking for?
faq.stillNeedHelpDesc: If you can't find the answer you're looking for, here are some ways to get help
faq.githubDiscussionsDesc: Ask questions and get community help
faq.q1: What is Solidis and how is it different from other Redis clients?
faq.a1: Solidis is a fast, zero-dependency RESP client for Redis and Valkey, written in strict TypeScript around SOLID principles.
faq.a2: Solidis is tested against Redis 6.2 and later and Valkey 7.2 and later, over both RESP2 and RESP3.
faq.q3: Can I use Solidis in production?
faq.a3: Yes. It reconnects automatically with configurable retries and backoff, fails in-flight commands at once on faults, and restores the session after a reconnect.
faq.q4: How does Solidis handle command pipelining?
faq.a4: Commands sent in the same tick go out as one pipeline, which cuts network round trips. maxCommandsPerPipeline (default 300) caps each pipeline.
faq.q5: What's the performance compared to other Redis clients?
faq.a5: Against {clients}, Solidis is the fastest in {wins} of {total} benchmarks and up to {peak} faster than the next-fastest client ({iterations} operations, {concurrency} concurrency).
faq.a6: Yes. client.multi() starts a transaction; queue commands, then call exec() to run them atomically.
faq.q7: How do I configure connection timeouts?
faq.a7: connectionTimeout (default 2000 ms) bounds connecting, and commandTimeout (default 5000 ms) bounds each command. Give one request its own timeout with client.send(commands, { timeout: 10000 }).
faq.a8: Set authentication: { username, password }. On Redis 6+ with ACL users, pass both.
faq.a9: Both RESP2 (default) and RESP3. Choose with the protocol option.
faq.q10: How do I handle connection errors?
faq.a10: Errors are typed, such as SolidisConnectionError, SolidisClientError and SolidisRequesterError, and linked by cause. Reconnects retry up to maxConnectionRetries (default 20) times, with a backoff that starts at connectionRetryDelay (default 100 ms).
faq.q11: Why am I getting timeout errors?
faq.a11: Usually network trouble, an overloaded server or a timeout set too short. Check connectionTimeout (default 2000 ms) and commandTimeout (default 5000 ms), and that the server responds.
faq.q12: How do I debug connection issues?
faq.a12: Set debug: true and listen with client.on('debug', (entry) => console.log(entry)) to log connection events, commands and errors.

architecture.title: Architecture Overview
architecture.subtitle: Understanding Solidis's internal structure and SOLID design principles.
architecture.coreDesc: Core entry point that creates and coordinates all components
architecture.coreRecovery: Session recovery after a reconnect: authentication, protocol, database and subscriptions
architecture.connReconnect: Automatic reconnection with configurable retry delay
architecture.requesterDesc: Handles command pipelining and request states
architecture.parserDesc: Processes RESP2/RESP3 protocol with optimized buffer handling
architecture.pubsubDesc: Maintains subscription state for Pub/Sub functionality
architecture.debugEvent: Entries delivered through the debug event
architecture.debugArguments: Entries name commands, never their arguments
architecture.srpDesc: Each component has a single, well-defined responsibility
architecture.srpExample: Parser only handles RESP protocol parsing, not connection management
architecture.ocpDesc: Open for extension through extend(), closed for modification
architecture.ocpExample: Add custom commands without modifying core client code
architecture.lspDesc: Components can be swapped for alternative implementations
architecture.lspExample: SolidisFeaturedClient extends SolidisClient and works wherever a SolidisClient is expected
architecture.dipDesc: Components depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations
architecture.dipExample: Command functions depend only on a send() method, not on the client class
architecture.flow1Desc: User calls a command method (e.g., client.set('key', 'value'))
architecture.flow2Desc: Command is added to the pipeline queue and serialized to the RESP protocol with its batch
architecture.flow3Desc: The serialized pipeline is written to the TCP socket
architecture.flow4Desc: Parser reads and parses RESP responses from Redis with binary-safe buffer handling
architecture.flow5Desc: Parsed response is matched to the original command and the promise is resolved
architecture.flow6Desc: The parsed result is returned to the user's await statement
architecture.systemArchitectureDesc: Overview of how Solidis components work together
architecture.solidDesc: Solidis follows SOLID design principles, so it is easy to maintain, test and extend.
architecture.commandFlowDesc: How commands flow through the Solidis architecture
architecture.perfDesc: The design decisions that make Solidis fast
architecture.binarySafeParserDesc: The parser reads socket chunks incrementally and never modifies them. Bulk replies are views of that data, so holding a Buffer reply keeps its chunk in memory.
architecture.pipelineBatchingDesc: Commands are batched into pipelines automatically to cut round trips; maxCommandsPerPipeline caps their size.
architecture.bufferMgmtDesc: Bulk replies are views of the received data, and each pipeline is serialized into one buffer, which keeps garbage collection low.
architecture.lazyConnDesc: With lazyConnect, the constructor does not connect; the client connects on connect() or on its first command.

apiReference.title: API Reference
apiReference.subtitle: Complete reference documentation for all Solidis classes, methods, and interfaces.
apiReference.mainClassDesc: The main client class for interacting with Redis servers
apiReference.connectDesc: Connects to the server and resolves once the client is ready. The constructor calls it unless lazyConnect is true, in which case the first command also connects. Commands sent before the client is ready wait for it.
apiReference.disconnectDesc: Closes the connection to the Redis server and cleans up resources.
apiReference.setDesc: Sets a key to hold the string value.
apiReference.getDesc: Gets the value of a key.
apiReference.transactionsDesc: A transaction runs a group of commands atomically, in one step, with MULTI/EXEC.
apiReference.pipelinesDesc: Pipelining sends several commands without waiting for replies, then reads all replies at once, which cuts round trips.
apiReference.pubsubDesc: Publishers send messages to channels, and subscribers of those channels receive them.
apiReference.customCommandsDesc: Add your own commands with extend() to build higher-level abstractions without touching the core.
apiReference.rawCommandsDesc: Run commands that have no method yet with send(). It sends them as given but refuses commands whose replies cannot be paired, such as MONITOR, SYNC and CLIENT REPLY OFF. Its timeout option replaces commandTimeout for that request; 0 disables it. Pass blockingTimeout with a raw blocking command such as BLPOP to handle it like blpop().
apiReference.binaryValuesDesc: Writes such as set, mset, hset, lpush and xadd store Buffer values byte for byte, publish and spublish take Buffer messages, and send() takes a Buffer for any argument. Reads decode UTF-8 unless you pass { buffer: true } to reads such as get, mget, hget, hgetall, lrange and blpop.
apiReference.bigIntegersDesc: Commands return integers as numbers and reject one past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, such as a TTL, with the exact bigint as cause. INCR, INCRBY, DECR, DECRBY, HINCRBY, BITFIELD and BITFIELD_RO take { bigint: true }, which always returns a bigint.
apiReference.debuggingDesc: Debug entries trace connection state, commands and errors.
apiReference.errorBase: Base error class for all Solidis errors
apiReference.errorCommand: Errors during command execution or reply handling
apiReference.errorExecution: Command timeouts and commands rejected before sending
apiReference.eventConnect: Emitted when the client connects to the server
apiReference.eventReady: Emitted when the client is ready to send commands
apiReference.eventClose: Emitted with the cause when the connection is lost
apiReference.eventReconnecting: Emitted with the attempt number and delay before each reconnect attempt
apiReference.eventReconnected: Emitted when a reconnect completes and the client is ready again
apiReference.eventDrain: Emitted when the socket's write buffer drains
apiReference.eventMessage: Emitted when a message is received on a subscribed channel
apiReference.eventShardMessage: Emitted when a message is received on a shard channel
apiReference.eventPatternMessage: Emitted when a message matches a subscribed pattern
apiReference.eventSubscription: Emitted with the channel or pattern and the subscription count when a subscription changes; psubscribe, ssubscribe and each unsubscribe event work the same way
apiReference.eventPush: Emitted for pushes that are not Pub/Sub messages, such as client tracking invalidations, including those RESP2 delivers on __redis__:invalidate
apiReference.eventDebug: Emitted when a debug event is logged
